trigger.authentication_note: Gmail dennis@work.flowers (the non-shared connection). The Gmail credential lives HERE, not in --connections — the workflow code never calls Gmail.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger, one run per EMAIL (not per attachment) — that is what lets the classifier see an invoice alongside the receipt that settles it. The query only narrows what Gmail polls; the authoritative filters are BLOCKED_SENDERS / BLOCKED_SUBJECTS / BLOCKED_LABELS in workflow.ts.

connectionless_apps.AICLIAPI: get_completion — authentication_id "0" (Included in Plan), no connection

ai_model.note: Tier drives task cost: standard 1x, advanced 3x, premium 5x tasks per run (plus the same multiplier per tool call; this step makes none). Those three sentinels are the only valid values — anything else errors with 'Unknown tier sentinel'. Standard reaches the same routing verdict as Advanced on every case in the README's verified table, including SimplePay's statement-history inference. Re-run those cases before changing tier.

description: Gmail email with PDF attachments -> classify every attachment in ONE AI by Zapier call (email context + all extracted PDF text) -> file each into Invoices / Paid Receipts / Signed Agreements / Financial Reporting. Migration of the classic 'Gmail Attachments to Google Drive by Type' Zap. The Invoices folder holds only outstanding bills: an invoice is withheld when a receipt on the same email settles it (matched on invoice number), when the classifier matches a sibling receipt on vendor+amount+date, when a sibling account statement shows the vendor auto-clearing every prior invoice with a same-day card payment, or when the invoice itself carries paid markers. The classic Zap's 'due date == invoice date' proxy is deliberately gone — due-on-receipt invoices are often genuinely unpaid.

version_history.note: Added the recurring-auto-charge signal (Auto-Paid By Recurring Charge) after SimplePay's monthly invoice+statement email filed to Invoices. No receipt exists in that email; the evidence is the statement's history of same-day card payments.

Model tier advanced/auto -> standard/auto (3x -> 1x tasks per run) after verifying identical routing verdicts on every test case. Also gated the superseded-by-receipt signal on a Receipt actually being present: on SimplePay the model reported it with only a statement attached, reaching the right verdict but recording evidence that did not exist.

SUPERSEDED same day by 019fdb72. Fixed ZAP-26 (StepExhaustedError in extract-text-0). Files by Zapier returns a PDF's RAW BYTES as 'text' when it cannot convert it and failOnConversionError:false stops it throwing; Wise's password-protected Monthly_Statement.pdf produced 128KB of binary containing 101 NULs, and checkpointing that step return to PostgreSQL failed with SQLSTATE 22P05 on all 5 retries. The checkpoint happens after the step returns, so the step's own try/catch could not see it. Added looksLikeRawFileBytes() to route undecoded file bytes onto the existing empty-text path, and stripUncheckpointableChars() to scrub NUL/C0/lone surrogates from anything leaving the step. Also blocked the subject 'your monthly statement for assets' to save the AI task on a statement that is never filed.

An attachment whose text could not be extracted is now NEVER filed, whatever it classifies as - encrypted, scanned, malformed or converted to empty text all stop at textExtracted:false with the reason 'no text could be extracted - not filed on filename and email evidence alone' and the underlying cause in the new textExtractionError output field. Dennis's call: classifying a document you cannot read is a guess off its filename and the surrounding email, and a guessed invoice in the Invoices folder is indistinguishable from a real bill. Unreadable attachments are also excluded from the sibling-evidence signals in decide(), so a filename-guessed 'Receipt' can no longer suppress a genuine outstanding invoice. They are still classified (the AI call is one per email, so a readable sibling pays for it anyway) and the verdict is recorded in run history. Accepted trade-off: a real unpaid bill arriving as a scan or encrypted PDF stays in Gmail only - fix that with OCR on extraction, not by relaxing this rule. Covered by 19 offline assertions over the real decide(), including every case in the README's verified table.
